Recording is already allowed, but Mika still can’t record. Check that the microphone access switch in Quick Settings is on (Android 12 and later), and that Mika’s microphone isn’t turned off in the system’s permission manager. Another app may also be using the microphone.

Speech to text is set to the phone’s built-in recognition, but this phone doesn’t have it now. Pick another one in Settings › Models › Speech to text.
The phone’s built-in speech recognition didn’t respond, so no words came through. Pick a provider’s speech model in Settings › Models › Speech to text and it will work.
The phone’s built-in speech recognition couldn’t start. Try again, or choose another recognition method in Settings › Models › Speech to text.
The phone’s speech recognition can’t record yet

“%1$s” is the app that does speech recognition on this phone, and it hasn’t been allowed to record audio, so it can’t hear you. Mika’s own microphone permission is fine. Open its permission page and turn on the microphone, then come back and hold to talk again. You can also choose another recognition method in Settings › Models › Speech to text.
Couldn’t open the settings page for “%1$s”. Find it in the system’s app list and turn on the microphone.
The provider of the chosen speech model has been removed. Pick another one in Settings › Models › Speech to text.
Speech to text is turned off. Pick one in Settings › Models › Speech to text.

Mika cần mic
To hear you while you hold to talk, Mika needs to record audio. It was denied before, so the phone won’t ask again. Turn on the microphone on Mika’s permission page in system settings.
